links.outcome: Harm-eliciting success rate of adversarial red-team prompts against a medical LLM assistant
links.effect: 11 of 160 adversarial prompts (6.9%) elicited clinically significant harm; full refusal in 86.2%; authority impersonation succeeded 45.0%, Educational Authority sub-strategy 83.3%; six of eight categories had no successful attacks.
links.quote: Of 160 adversarial prompts evaluated against Claude Sonnet 4.5, 11 (6.9%) elicited responses meeting our threshold for clinically significant harm (harm level ≥ 3 on a 0–5 scale).

links.outcome: Multi-turn escalation attack success rate against the medical assistant
links.effect: Multi-turn escalation attacks achieved 0% success (0/20), while authority impersonation prompts elicited harmful responses in 45.0% of cases.

unlisted_practices: Physician review of automated evaluator-flagged high-harm responses
Context-conditioned guardrail design targeting authority impersonation (claims of educational or professional context)

screen.reason: Empirical study systematically evaluating and red-teaming safety guardrails (including standard medical assistant system prompts) of LLMs under clinical adversarial attacks.
